verdict.rationale: Sardine documents that users can tune fuzzy-match thresholds to balance true and false positives, which covers configuring name matching. It also mentions explainable scores and routing matches to analysts for review. Nothing in the evidence addresses alias or transliteration matching, or how an analyst would inspect why a name matched. Missing for 10: documented alias/AKA matching, transliteration or cross-script name matching, a match-detail inspection view showing alias or transliteration reasons, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a risk-analyst, I can configure name matching and inspect alias or transliteration matches

citations.quote: We allow you to tweak the thresholds for fuzzy matches such that you can balance the trade-off between true positives and false positive alerts.
Auto-clear low-risk matches and escalate real exposure with explainable scores.
route higher-risk matches for analyst review
